Hi [~accountid:6411c587f1b529dfa98c0e66],

I don’t see any immediate red flags, but there are a couple of things to keep in mind:

* *Clause 4* allows for additional fees to be charged if the scope of the work expands due to unforeseen complexities or errors.
* *Clause 4.7* stipulates that if you choose to terminate the agreement before its completion, you will still be liable for payment for services rendered up to the point of termination. For fixed-fee services, this will be calculated based on the time spent at the then-current hourly rates, plus any incurred expenses.

That said, have you reviewed the contract yourself? Are you comfortable with the scope of services and UHY's responsibilities outlined in it?

Many thanks!

My view re/ the user:

It's a professional complainer - the core of all complaints comes down to lawsuit threats and coercion to get money from Bolt as compensation from the very beginning - [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-31147|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-31147|smart-link] .

I do not see this as high risk due to the fact that his claims are unsubstantiated. Details: 

* Complaints revolved around: (i) not being able to unsubscribe; (ii) alleging marketing violations under the GDPR, CPRA, and Israel privacy laws, such as not including disclaimer “Advertising” in our DM.
* From the very beginning, the focus was - the demand to compensate him for “damages” to settle the problem “peacefully” - originally, he demanded 1500 EUR, his claim gradually rose to 13 million EUR.
* Importantly: we have no records of attempts to unsubscribe from his accounts via unsubscribe links & communication preferences. This was checked and double checked with LCM and martech.

I suggest to respond with the following and close the matter:

{quote}_Dear Mr. Bocobza,_

_Please note that the ultimate data controller responsible for data processing activities in the EU, including direct marketing, is our Estonian entity, Bolt Operations OU. You can find the complete list of Bolt group companies and controllers via this link:_ [_https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-controller-list/_|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-controller-list/]_._

_Please let us know if there are any outstanding issues with you receiving direct marketing from Bolt - we appreciate your collaboration to resolve the issue. Please note that each of our emails includes an unsubscribe link, and you can also unsubscribe using the Communication Preferences in the app._

_Best regards,_

_Bolt`s Privacy Team_{quote}

If we actually receive a claim anywhere in the jurisdictions the complainant is threatening us with and get notified - we will deal with this separately.

A comment from [~accountid:5d8df271090bd70dc49aed3c] , based on his research:

*Cache mode*
NJSC already exposes {{CacheStrategyRedis}} abstraction which essentially is the {{usage: cache}} enum value from the above proposal.
This abstraction enforces the setting of the key expiration time.
Consequently, the users of this abstraction must handle the missing key due to expiration time; to my findings, some of the services refresh the key, and some just ignore/log a message.
{{grep "new CacheStrategyRedis"}} returns {{364}} places. It's not clear to how many Redis instances they are bound to, but looks like a massive usage of the cache pattern.
*No Key Expiration*
A few services use RedisConnection directly, and I found {{16}} places that do NOT set the key expiration time.
So, it looks like these services use Redis as persistent storage, but there are only few services in this situation.*Conclusions*

* In terms of additional NJSC abstractions, together with [@juri|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U5S3RGL66], we think NJSC provides enough Redis/Caching abstractions.
* Migrating eviction policy from volatile-ttl to allkeys-lru looks more like a communication exercise, so all the affected teams will be aware some keys can be evicted more aggressively; anyway the majority of the services expect the keys to expire, and handle the situation according with their business requirements.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *10 November 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/?category=rides|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;

* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

Eaters are reaching out to CS due to an anxiety, which is stemming from below reasons:

# They think they were charged for an order they didn’t receive,
# They can not see their order in the app,
# They are not aware of pre-authentification.
# They are seeking clarification what will happen next (Will the order be accepted and delivered? How can they get their money back?)



Most often, due unawareness of reserving money pre order, *eaters think they were charged incorrectly, because the order didn't go through and is not visible in the app order history*. However, they can see money taken from their bank account. They can not see a status for their order, because it is not recorded in the app, since it didn’t go through. Due to this, eaters often repeat their order, which end up the same way, hence they claim the they were charged twice for the order. Also, in case of payment processing issues, there is no further communication that in case of a not delivered order, reserved money will be transferred back to their bank account.

After CS has educated eaters on pre-authentification and assured the money will be released after 1-14 days, eaters' anxiety resolves and tickets can be closed.



This is causing unnecessary anxiety and CS tickets. If we let eaters know about pre-authentification proactively, this would probably reduce CS tickets about pre-auth issues. *We can see from the tickets that simple explanation and assurance about releasing the money satisfies eaters.*

Moreover, we could better focus on analysing reasons for failed payments and charging eaters twice, as there were examples in the sample where eaters reported they can’t pay (one reason was a Russian card for example) and where courier asked for an extra cash payment (for delivering into nearby address).

[~accountid:712020:85a31a38-edb2-4253-b037-fa5bcad14728] could you please clarify the business reasons for not allowing fleet owners to work as couriers?

My immediate thoughts on this are the following:

* Allowing fleet owners to work as couriers may generally lead to an increase of reclassification risk since the legal entity and the individual are in practice the same.
* However, in MT LOPS has already decided to work with self-employed couriers and I would not reckon the risk of reclassification of fleet owners to be higher from self-employed couriers.
* Additionally, the risk is limited to fleet managers and hence the liability would be ring fenced to a small number of individuals.
* Therefore, provided that the fleet owner fulfils the requirements to register as a courier in Bolt Food, I would from a reclassification point of view consider onboarding these individuals as risky as onboarding self-employed couriers and the risk limited to the specific individuals in this situation.

Thank you.

* ATO T&Cs ([https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-driver/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-driver/?category=rides|smart-link] )
** Agency clauses must be clear, i.a. in the sense that it must be clear which legal entity gives authorisation to whom.
** We know that practically Bolt Operations OÜ manages payments and must be authorised as the commercial agent by the seller. 
** Definition of Bolt is extremely wide, and includes Bolt Operations OÜ and its affiliates; as well as Bolt Services RO SRL. ← Not clear what the operating setup actually is. What is the role of Bolt Services RO SRL, and does Bolt Operations OÜ have similar role as app/platform provider, as elsewhere. Let’s discuss this on a call, if makes more sense.
** Clause 1.15 translation is the following “1.15. Payment Agent – ​​Bolt Operations OÜ, a private limited liability company established and registered in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Estonia, with the Commercial Register registration number 14532901, with its registered office at Vana-Lõuna tn 15/1, Tallinn 10134, Republic of Estonia, i.e. the agent responsible for technical support related to payment services that facilitate payments and/or invoicing on behalf of Bolt. The Payment Agent may also discuss any complaints and resolve any disputes arising in connection with payments.” ← We should not use the term “payment agent”. Need to check whether it is the same in local language.
** Clause “6.1. We allow Passengers to pay for Transportation Services by card, cash, and other payment methods (Bolt for Business, etc.) directly in the Bolt app (i.e. In-app Payment). You hereby authorize us to act as your commercial agent in a limited manner only for the purpose of collecting, on your behalf, the Fare or other fees paid by the Passenger via the In-app Payment method. Any payment obligation paid by the Passenger via the In-app Payment method will be deemed fulfilled as of the date of payment.” ← This does not comply with requirements to commercial agent exemption related clauses
* Driver T&Cs ([https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/terms-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/terms-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link] ).
** Similar issues as above.
* Passenger T&Cs ([https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-rider/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-rider/?category=rides|smart-link] ):
** Similar comment. Definition of Bolt is extremely wide, and includes Bolt Operations OÜ and its affiliates; as well as Bolt Services RO SRL.
** Clause “3.1 You can pay for transportation services by card, but also by other payment methods (for example: Bolt Business), which require prior activation of the function in the Bolt app. By providing the Bolt in-App Payment service, Bolt acts as a commercial agent for alternative transportation service operators. Each provider has authorized Bolt as a commercial agent for the conclusion of contracts between the provider and the passenger, including the authorization to accept payments from passengers and to transmit payments to the provider. Your obligation to the alternative transportation service operator will be fulfilled when the payment order for the transfer of funds to Bolt’s bank account is issued. You, as a passenger, are responsible for ensuring that the payment is made and that there are sufficient funds available for it.” ← Referring back to the definition, it is not clear which entity has been authorised as seller’s commercial agent. This may be an issue of translation, but the wording of the clause is very weird (e.g. “the payment order for the transfer of funds to Bolt’s bank account is issued”).

h2. model-invoker - Analysis on 24 hours data

The chart with highest total requests shows significant spikes in request volume, particularly during peak times. Now this is also due to [+Two-step batching for Instant orders+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BF/pages/5083758620/EXP+-+2024.06+Two-step+batching+for+Instant+orders], as we can see there load starts and ends at specific times. This indicates that the service might face bottlenecks. Within a single parallel call, the endpoint frequently processes between 6 and 10 requests during peak times, which is most likely only 10 during that time.

Conclusions on current configuration:

* {{max_parallel_requests: 20}} shows the endpoint can handle concurrent calls to some extent, but the spikes might overwhelm this configuration, especially when requests per minute exceed a certain threshold
* {{max_elements_per_request: 10}} balances batching efficiency with potential latency trade-offs. However, during high-traffic spikes, smaller batches might help spread the load more effectively.

Proposal:

* Keep {{max_elements_per_request}} at 10: This matches traffic profile in most of the cases observed.
* If possible, adjust {{max_parallel_requests}} dynamically:
** For peak hours, increase to 25–30 to handle more concurrent calls, or after [+Two-step batching for Instant orders+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BF/pages/5083758620/EXP+-+2024.06+Two-step+batching+for+Instant+orders] is officially launched
** For non-peak hours, the value can stay as is

Hey folks! There is no new workload coming to CS 🙂 Previously, _all_ merchant support requests were attributed to the *Provider* persona and processed by CS. Now we have created a new persona – *Provider Lead* and will attribute requests sent by merchants that have not yet been activated on Bolt Food to it. So, we are just splitting the same requests in a different manner. 

The idea behind this split is that merchants in the onboarding stage have very different problems and questions compared to active merchants. We are currently running an experiment in PT, GH, UA to learn more about the specifics of these requests. By mid-February we should be able to use the collected info to build a new knowledge base infoset for CS agents to process the requests of onboarding merchants in a more efficient manner.

There are 5 sales reps in PT, GH, UA who have agreed to play the role of CS agents to help us gather the info during this experiment’s timeframe. If they encounter a situation when a request has been sent by a merchant in the onboarding state but it has nothing to do with the onboarding, they will be changing the persona for these requests to *Provider* so that they can be processed by CS as usually. 

Please, let me know if you have questions left. We can also have a call 🙂

Hi [~accountid:6052891966c87900682ac4e9] [~accountid:62455ffb7a3f9e006ab25c60] , I’ve taken a look at this and would like to provide some initial guidance from Privacy POV.

----

{color:#0747a6}*_tl;dr: It depends - for how long do we want to store data?_* {color}🤔 

----

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*General context - retention schedule*
{panel}

First off, our Global Retention Schedule project is still ongoing and is anticipated to complete only by end of 2025. However, *that should not stop us from defining a reasonable retention period for communications data now*. Any decision we make at this point can later be incorporated into the retention schedule.

It’s also important to highlight that the Privacy Team’s scope primarily concerns the *retention of personal data*. This means that while we may provide guidance on data containing personal data, *retention of non-personal, anonymized, or aggregated data is not dictated by privacy laws* in the same way. In other words, if the data is not personal (identifiable), privacy laws won’t apply.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Questions*
{panel}

To move forward, I’d like to clarify a few points:

# *Nature of lifecycle comms:*
#* Can we confirm exactly which categories of communications we’re dealing with (e.g., marketing emails, transactional emails, operational announcements, legal notifications such as updates to Terms & Conditions)? [~accountid:62455ffb7a3f9e006ab25c60] 
#* Is there a document or spreadsheet that details the specific types of communications under consideration, including the personal data they might contain? [~accountid:62455ffb7a3f9e006ab25c60] 
# *Scope/extent of involvement of personal data:*
#* How much of the data within these communications is actually personal (e.g., identifiable user information)? [~accountid:62455ffb7a3f9e006ab25c60] 
#* Are we talking about full email content that identifies individual recipients, or would the content be general, with no direct link back to a user? [~accountid:62455ffb7a3f9e006ab25c60] 

*What could the retention periods be?*

From a legal standpoint in Europe (including the UK, France, Portugal, Spain, and broadly under the GDPR), there is *no single mandated retention period* for all types of communications. Instead, the overarching principle is one of purpose limitation and data minimization:
* We should only retain personal data for as long as is necessary to fulfill the original purpose for which it was collected.
* Once the purpose is fulfilled (e.g., after a reasonable time window to handle disputes or queries, or after a statutory limitation period for consumer complaints), we should delete or anonymize that data.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*In practice, there’s a tendency to align retention periods for communications with:*
{panel}

* *Statutory limitation periods for legal claims* (often 3-6 years in many EU jurisdictions, depending on the nature of the claim).
* *Regulatory expectations to demonstrate compliance with consent or contract terms* (e.g., retaining evidence that a user agreed to T&Cs, or that certain information was communicated within a required timeframe).

*Next Steps:*

* Identify exactly which communications contain personal data and which do not.

Hi [~accountid:617a82d4b9c549006fffb227]  thanks for raising the ticket. 

Please find below my thoughts on the feature. 

*Dispatching logic* 

Key element is the dispatching logic. Considering FR is a high reclass risk country I recommend to implement a dispatching based on a objective criteria such as radius and ETA. All drivers must be treated the same and you should refrain from dispatching based on drivers KPIs/past performance. 



*Regulatory constraints*

Feature could lead to a "fastest finger first" competition where drivers may feel rushed to accept requests, leading to hasty decisions and increased cancellations. Please bear in mind that according to the relevant transportation code provisions drivers should be able to refuse orders as much as they want with no consequences on their accounts.



As long as drivers can freely accept/ refuse ride orders as much as they want and dispatching relies on objective metrics (radius/eta), feature roll out does not pose major risks. 

Thanks,

Michela

If no personal data is being shared between the parties in regards to this partnership, then the section 10 in Annex 1 is irrelevant. At the moment these clauses deem Bolt as the processor of personal data on behalf of Lidl. Therefore for example giving very broad auditing rights to Lidl ( granting access to documents containing assessments of the observance of the personal data protection and security requirements, as well as to +grant access to its business premises+ and bearing the costs of such audits). In addition if Bolt does not fulfill the obligations regarding personal data protection as mentioned in the agreement, it will have to pay damages in a quantum equal to the prejudice that Lidl suffered. 

If Bolt is not providing services which includes processing personal data then section 10 should be removed from Annex 1. We cannot commit to such obligations when this does not actually reflect the context of the partnership. If any personal data is being processed/shared by the parties, then such clauses should correctly reflect the data flow and roles and responsibilities of the parties within the specific processing activities.

Hello Oana,

Getting back to your request: first of all, it is important to differentiate between Demerit Decay and the Investigation Outcome. When we calculate demerit decay, the cases in the same grouping are to be counted: 

* *Low and Moderate Risk Events* will decay after 3 months.
* *High Risk Events* will decay after 12 months.
* *Significant Risk Events* will not decay.

However, when it comes to making a final decision on the investigation outcome, we need to take a *full picture of the profile*, not just the cases in the same grouping. That is why we need to check for cases outside of the grouping to see other previous reports and decide how to proceed. 

Let me know if any questions arise!

Galina

Hey [~accountid:639212cda593cb822e99192b] , thanks so much for this. Main points I’d like to raise:

* I’d still like to know where we’re taking postal codes from. Do we come up with them by checking the user’s pick-up point location? Or do we take it from elsewhere?
* It’s important to consider the level of detail postal codes provide, especially given global variations in their formats. If we share only a broad postal area - one that doesn’t pinpoint a specific address - then we’re on safer ground. However, in less densely populated regions, there could be only a single house on a street. Then, a postal code might effectively identify a specific house.
** This raises a potential privacy concern: by sharing what may seem like non-identifying data, we could inadvertently reveal more than intended.

Bottom line - I don’t see privacy being a blocker for this initiative. However, we need to check what postal codes mean, anonymize them sufficiently, and clarify where we’re taking this data from.

        search_category_id,
        connection_id
    FROM

    WHERE

),
search_category AS (
    SELECT 
        id, 
        name 
    FROM 
        ng_rental.rental_fleet_search_category
),
marker_mask_changes AS (
    -- Step 2: Identify marker mask changes where 2147483648 was added
    SELECT
        vse.vehicle_id,
        vse.created AS change_time,
        vse.value AS new_marker_mask,
        LAG(vse.value) OVER (PARTITION BY vse.vehicle_id ORDER BY vse.created) AS old_marker_mask,
        vse.connection_id
    FROM
        ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event AS vse
    WHERE
        vse.type = 'marker_mask'
        AND bitwise_and(vse.value, CAST(2147483648 AS BIGINT)) > 0
),
latest_marker_mask_addition AS (
    -- Step 3: Get the latest marker mask addition
    SELECT
        vehicle_id,
        change_time AS last_change_time,
        connection_id
    FROM
        marker_mask_changes
    WHERE
        bitwise_and(old_marker_mask, CAST(2147483648 AS BIGINT)) = 0
        OR old_marker_mask IS NULL
),
theft_event_details AS (
    -- Step 4: Get the details of theft events after the latest marker mask addition
    SELECT 
        vse.vehicle_id,
        MAX(vse.created) AS created,
        MAX(vse.value) AS value,
        MAX(vse.lat) AS lat,
        MAX(vse.lng) AS lng,
        vse.connection_id
    FROM 
        ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event AS vse
    JOIN 
        latest_marker_mask_addition AS lma
    ON 
        vse.vehicle_id = lma.vehicle_id
        AND vse.created >= lma.last_change_time
        AND vse.connection_id = lma.connection_id
    WHERE 
        vse.type = 'marker_mask'
        AND bitwise_and(vse.value, CAST(2147483648 AS BIGINT)) > 0
    GROUP BY 
        vse.vehicle_id, 
        vse.connection_id
),
battery_state AS (
    SELECT 
        bs.state,
        bs.battery_id
    FROM 
        ng_rental.rental_battery_report_battery_state AS bs
)
-- Step 5: Combine the results with vehicle state
SELECT 
    vs.vehicle_id,
    ted.created AS time_of_theft,
    ted.lat AS theft_location_lat,
    ted.lng AS theft_location_lng,
    bs.battery_id AS current_vehicle_battery_id,
    bs.state AS current_vehicle_battery_state,
    sc.name AS search_category_name
FROM

INNER JOIN

ON

LEFT JOIN

    search_category AS sc

Adding some more context for the Ridehailing vertical:

Pre-auth is used according to fraud rules. There are 2 mains scenarios:

# In some markets we do pre-auth for 100% of users. This is the case in London, Paris, South Africa and some other high fraudulent markets
# In others (eg: Baltics) we do pre-auth only to certain users according to Fraud rules. It can be new users, or users using a new payment method, using international cards or simply users that had failed payments before, etc

{quote}We pre-auth when a rider books a taxi, right?{quote}

* Yes
* User selects destination, we:
** Pre-authorize amount
** If succeeded, find user a driver
*** If not, show error message

{quote}_Do you know when this charge becomes official?_{quote}

* Debit/credit cards work with a mechanism of _Authorization_ and _Capture._ The first holds funds from user bank account, the second is the confirmation of a transaction. A pre-authorization is a simple authorization. At the end of the order the capture happens

Answer from DB support:
{{Full table scan}} is expected in this case, because the subquery is treated as a derived table (a temporary result set stored in memory or a temporary table on disk with no indexes), MySQL must scan all of its rows. Hence, the EXPLAIN plan shows an “ALL” table access type for the derived table, indicating a full scan of that derived result set.

*My feedback:*

* *Unclear communication:* The information provided does not align with the driver’s query, as they are asking about a discrepancy in their balance.
* *Closing issues:* The building block flow was not followed, and the proper closing was not completed. Examples: “Que tengas buena tarde” or “Que tengas buen resto de jornada.”
* *Incorrect information/education:* The agent stated that all payments accumulated in the balance are used to pay commissions, which is incorrect. Drivers can withdraw this money to their bank account. Additionally, the statement, “These payments are credited to your balance within the same day,” implies that payments are received on the same day, while in reality, payments are processed on Mondays each week and can take up to 72 hours to be credited.
* *Knowledge base:* The KB does not reference user discounts, which should be reflected in the driver’s balance.

h3. *Quality Team Feedback*

*Scorecard section:*

* *Seamless Interaction, Relevant Information & Questions:* The information itself is clear, but it does not cover the initial topic or answer the driver’s question.
* *Issue Tagging:* Another correct tag would be "I have a question about the rider's promotion."
* The information for the case could be found here.

*Comment section:*
There are several elements listed, but the first piece in bold does not show one. Instead, it’s the reason why "Seamless Interaction" was rated down. For better clarity, I’d suggest using bold font for elements only.

* {color:#ff991f}*Anlysis.*{color}
- *Improvement points:*

In this particular feedback, I would give a more empathetic written response, as the Confluence article _Communicating Quality Feedback to Suppliers_ explains.
** *Tone & Empathy:* I would give a *👎🏻* on “Too formal / informal or unnatural tone / language” because the written message sounds robotic and almost macro-like. Our goal is to have a friendly conversation and for the user to feel like they are being assisted by a human.
** *Relevant Information & Questions:* I would give a *👎🏻* on Missing information / education, since as you mentioned, the KB _Driver: I have a question about the rider's promotion_ is more aligned with the driver’s question. With the proper investigation, the user could have been better informed.
** *Issue tagging:* I would give a *👎🏻* on Missing issue tags, since, as you mentioned, another issue tag related to the case is "I have a question about the rider's promotion."

Info I received:
Our plan is to issue invoices in the official language of the country where the service is provided. This has been discussed at length with legal and tax departments. For this business, it will mean that they will receive invoices in Slovak for trips made in Slovakia, regardless of the language their employee has selected in the app.

But for trips made abroad, it will mean they will receive invoices in the local language of the market where the trips took place. Not in Slovak. And we will not make exceptions. It’s normal that, in Poland, the invoice will be in Polish. That in the UK, the invoice will be in English. Just like any other invoice provided by local businesses (which drivers are) will be in the language of the country.

If the above doesn’t work for them, alternative would be to switch to resale in which case they will get the aggregate invoice once a month from Bolt.

Thank you for reaching out to us! Do you mean assuming the gender by observation of the candidate during an interview? 

If yes, then this raises both legal and ethical concerns. Even if we use the data in an aggregated form later, then we would still have the gender data in an identifiable form. Recording or marking a candidate's gender based on assumptions or observations can lead to bias, even if unintentionally. Gender identity can be a sensitive topic and it is generally considered respectful to avoid making assumptions about someone's gender based on their appearance. In cases where a data subject asks for their data, we would have to disclose all the markups/notes done during the recruitment process, including the marked gender. In case we have “misgendered” the candidate, then in addition to privacy concerns this could have harmful consequences on our reputation. 

So as a general principle, disclosing the gender should be voluntary for the candidate and they can self-identify themselves (as it is now with the demographic survey). If the problem is low completion of the survey, then maybe we can explore changing the flow somehow? Asking less questions or maybe adding the questions at a later stage of the application?

However, the challenge will be implementing it within our dbt projects and our data platform architecture. It’s not a pattern that’s currently available in dbt by default. There are some nicely described attempts how to implement it using macros. The error is a normal ‘timed out' situation that’s experienced by one of the consumer when the broker goes offline.
It looks the KafkaJS client does its job as expected and presumably according with the configurations (timeout, max_retries), it just says cannot connect to this broker which is expected since the broker is down.  

*Expected Result*
*”Graceful Kafka broker restart should not have business impact, all partitions receive leaders before Kafka broker goes down.“*
This is the end-to-end system expectation; while KafkaJS library plays a crucial role it cannot guarantees alone the expectation since it depends on how it’s used by the upper levels in the stack. 

With the current data, this is not a KafkaJS bug, but more a recovery-time topic for the rides kafka cluster.
The end-to-end recovery-time depends on several variables controlled by different domain teams in the full stack. 
*Rides team*

* KafkaJS client configuration 
* The number of the consumer groups
* The number of producers and consumers
* Throughput, maybe?!

*PINT*

* Framework tooling as NJSC wraps KafkaJS  
** Strict and correct mapping between app layer configuration and correspondent KafkaJS parameters  
** Monitoring
** Logging/Error Handling

*SRE*

* Kafka Brokers cpu/mem/procs.


These being said, I suggest a distinct initiative in a joint effort team (SRE, PINT, Rides) whose ultimate goal would be to come up with a reference/baseline for the recovery time in the given _close_ to real conditions. 
There is nothing PINT can tackle alone here.

Hi [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] ,

Thank you! The first part of the questions has been requested from Gem, and I will share their responses with you as soon as I receive them.

In the meantime, here are the answers regarding the purposes for which GEM is utilized in the recruitment process:

# _Use of “AI Bots” to gather profiles actively from the internet_*_._* _Does this mean GEM scrapes data from publicly available sources and creates prospective candidate profiles for Bolt? -_ *GEM scrapes data from publicly available sources  from the internet to propose candidates*
# _Help filter /automatically review CVs / recommend who should be advanced/rejected_*_._* _Is it integrated with Greenhouse and we send the data to GEM for processing? On what criteria is this automatic filtering based? Does GEM provide a summary on the reasons why a certain candidate should be rejected before the recruiter takes the decision? -_ Y*es, GEM is integrated with Greenhouse, and it can support recruiters in managing the candidate pipeline. However, GEM does not automatically filter or recommend candidates to advance or reject. The integration allows for seamless syncing of candidate data from Greenhouse, but the decision-making process on who should proceed or be rejected is still managed by the recruiter, not GEM. GEM does not provide a summary specifically for why a candidate should be rejected. The decision to reject a candidate is made by the recruiter based on the candidate's profile, performance in interviews, and other criteria set in Greenhouse. GEM helps recruiters manage candidate relationships and track interactions but does not play a direct role in rejection summaries.*
# _CRM functionalities_*_._* _Is everything we store in Greenhouse also stored in GEM in order to manage the candidate relationship, including all the communication with the candidate?" -_ *No, GEM does not store everything from Greenhouse. While GEM is integrated with Greenhouse and syncs relevant candidate information, it focuses more on managing ongoing candidate relationships and engagement. Communication with candidates, such as emails, messages, and interactions tracked in GEM, is stored within the GEM platform itself. However, the full candidate profile, application details, and recruitment pipeline are managed in Greenhouse. Essentially, GEM acts as an engagement tool to track conversations, nurture candidates, and keep them engaged throughout the hiring process, while Greenhouse manages the actual recruiting workflow and candidate data.*

Thank you!

Dear Saad,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 17 November 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including the rights of passengers). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore share copies of your personal data to which you are entitled. Please note that in relation to your payment information as a fleet driver, payments are not made directly to fleet drivers by Bolt; instead, they are processed through their respective fleets. To access such information, we recommend reaching out to your fleet for assistance. They will be able to provide you with the necessary information regarding your earnings and payment disbursement.

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Your sincerely,

*Bolt*

Hi Patrícia, thank you for reaching out!

Firstly, you mentioned having *more guidelines on when compensation should be issued* - we already have the compensation guide that shows if you should compensate. It is currently rolled out in several markets (Portugal included), and soon will be rolled out globally. The compensation guide decides whether you have to compensate or not and there’s no need for any additional decisions. * 🚗[ Rider: Experience with my driver didn't meet my expectations |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/61980]
* 🚗 [Rider: My driver was impolite|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/68767]

Furthermore, I agree with you that customers often want to know *more information from us*, especially about the actions we are going to take against the driver. However, it’s usually *internal information* that can’t be shared with users. The most we can do is ensure the customer that we will take the action, without specifying the details. You can discuss this further with the Quality team, to get their advice.

*Relying on the rating the rider left* for the driver wouldn’t be an optimal solution, because we can’t be sure that the rider left the correct rating or selected it accidentally, also sometimes riders forget to leave it at all, and our actions shouldn’t depend on that. Also, we can’t share with riders that their rating affects driver scores, as this is internal information. Moreover, I don’t see how sharing that we will inform the Fleet owner would help in this case.

You also mentioned *escalating driver behavior issues to the OPS team* - that’s not necessary, as with BQS the OPS teams are notified automatically, they have the reports that show data on driver’s behavior.

So currently, I don’t see any opportunities to edit the process, and as you already mentioned - the empathizing and apologizing part should be discussed with the Quality team.

{quote}In the 🚗 🛴 [Rider: I was charged twice for my order|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013847979?country=global&language=en] process we have a section for cases when rider paid twice to the driver via the direct mobile payment. And one of the solutions is to inform the rider that the ride was paid using a payment method outside the app that we don’t have any control over, thus we can’t make a refund.{quote}

So all in all, my advice for refunding the overcharges:

* *Rider paid in-app and was overcharged*: refund the overcharged amount to the card (if partial refunds to the original payment method are available in Dubai)
* *Rider paid cash and was overcharged*: use the campaign enrollment of max possible amount
* *Rider paid in-app + was overcharged in cash*: 
** If there’s proof and payment is confirmed - give partial refund of max possible amount to org. payment method
** If not confirmed - do not issue any compensation

Data is also mapped to campaign enrolments i.e we get all the sessions from users who are enrolled in the city and campaigns of interest (DEX)

We have the following features for each of the session

* (Avg, Top3 avg, best, lowest) Surge multiplier and ETA
* Supply availability
* Timestamp of session
* User historical aggregations (Conversion, orders, Alive probability )

Future improvements:

* Historical age. conversion of geo/time units
* Extract more user level features about whether their affinity to time and geo
* Usage of non-DEX treatments (control groups for eg) over longer time window to improve the conversion model fit


Note: The behaviour of users (when and how often they do sessions) can differ when we use dynamic campaigns (specifying the range of discounts instead of fixed discounts). The regular DEX + corresponding sessions could be a reasonable proxy for us to start modelling  (DEX sets using dynamic campaigns is a bit tricky and may take time to collect too)

Or can there be any potential legal consequences when the data is deleted after the case is closed? Bolt’s [Whistleblower Policy |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/3500212316/Whistleblower+Policy]doesn’t specify the retention periods as well as I can see. 

So all in all, I would recommend the shortest data retention period if we don’t have any purpose/legal requirement to retain the data longer.

David,

Unfortunately, changing the way we compensate wouldn’t be a solution here, because we are talking about compensations for payments made outside the app. So in general, we shouldn’t even be compensating that. As I mentioned previously, we don’t track such payments, as well as we don’t know the verbal agreements between driver/rider. Allowing agents to compensate unlimited amounts after rider paid directly to driver would lead to fraud, and we would be giving out amounts that are not related to our ride prices.

So I just want to separate the 2 scenarios here:

* *Overcharges related to the ride price* (e.g. in-app payment ends up being higher than expected; cash payment is higher because the ride price increased) - we compensate to Bolt Balance/card/give discount.
* *Overcharges done outside the app, not related to ride price* - we shouldn’t be compensating. We have to take action against driver for fraudulent behavior, but we are not obligated to compensate the payment outside the app.
** The exception here is double payment - when rider paid in-app + gave the driver ride price in cash. Then we can refund the in-app payment.

One possible solution I see here is advising the rider to contact the driver directly via the app (in 24hrs) and agree to get their money back, as they paid directly to them and we are not related to this payment.
We also need around 2mw of BE effort for this one.

Hi all! 



I am not sure how this topic is regulated in PT. However, I will list here some of the assumptions that I think are relevant to how we handle this matter (please, confirm or rebute my assumptions). 

* All vehicles require a motor insurance policy - this will cover any damage to third-parties. 
* In most WE countries the driver/vehicle/FO have to hold a private hire licence. - Is this true in PT?) 
* Private hire licence often includes a requirement of additional insurance that would also cover passengers in the vehicle (this can be bought separately, or as a top off to motor insurance). It varies with regulation but this obligation might be imposed on either drivers, vehicle proprietors, or FOs. - Does PT regulation have such requirement? 

If my assumptions are true, then it should not be up to the FO to decide whether to decline or not. Furthermore, often the operator (us) has a due diligence obligation - i.e. we have to make sure that the driver/vehicle are licenced and meet all the licence requirements as well - that is why, in many markets we ask the private hire insurance as a part of the onboarding process and retain it in our admin. - If we also do that in PT, then we should have the insurer details on our files. 

If we have the insurer details on our files - we can escalate the claim directly to the insurer (leaving out the middle step with the FOs - the benefit of this, in my opinion, is a leaner process, and having fewer parties involved in data processing). 

In Bolt’s practice, claims escalation happens in two ways: either Bolt escalates the claim on behalf of the rider/user/third party, or Bolt forwards the insurers’ details to the injured party (however, in these cases Bolt is the policy holder for the insurer - so the privacy regulation is probably different - cc [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] ) 



*In short (and subject to my assumptions above): if we have the FOs insurer details in our admin, we should share the insurer’s details with the injured party. Insurer’s claims handlers are professionals who should not cause any further distress to the injured party, so this should alleviate the suffering of the riders, without causing any privacy implications.* 



However, if my assumptions are incorrect, let’s revise 🙂 



Best 

Karmel

{code:sql}WITH all_data AS (
SELECT DISTINCT
uor.created_date,
uor.order_country AS country_code,
uor.order__payment_method_type AS payment_method_type,
uor.decision,
uor.pre_auth_amount,
CASE WHEN uor.pre_auth_amount = 0 THEN 0 WHEN uor.pre_auth_amount > 0 THEN 1 END AS is_pre_auth,
uor.calculation_id,
uor.order_token_id AS session_id,
COALESCE(CAST(sco.rh_session_id AS varchar), CAST(uor.order_token_id AS varchar)) AS ultimate_session_id,
MAX(etl.id) OVER (PARTITION BY COALESCE(CAST(sco.rh_session_id AS varchar), CAST(uor.order_token_id AS varchar))) AS order_happened,
COALESCE(MIN(i.order__price_prediction_eur) OVER (PARTITION BY COALESCE(CAST(sco.rh_session_id AS varchar), CAST(uor.order_token_id AS varchar))),0) AS price_prediction_eur,
etl.user_id,
etl.user_price_eur,
etl.partner_price_eur,
etl.order_state,
etl.is_chargeback,
etl.is_payment_problem,
etl.is_final_failed_payment,
etl.potential_fraud_loss_eur + CASE WHEN etl.propagated_chargeback = TRUE THEN etl.card_captured_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate ELSE 0 END AS potential_fraud_loss_eur
FROM ng_public.etl_user_order_request_view AS uor
LEFT JOIN core.search_categories_overview AS sco
ON sco.search_token = uor.order_token_id
AND sco.created_hour >= DATE('2024-06-30') 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
ON etl.fraud_calculation_id = uor.calculation_id
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.created_date >= DATE('2024-07-01')
LEFT JOIN ng_pii.etl_user_order_request i ON i.id = uor.calculation_id AND i.created_date >= date '2024-07-01'
WHERE uor.created_date >= DATE('2024-07-01')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,12,13,14,15,16,17,18,19,etl.id,i.order__price_prediction_eur
)
SELECT
DATE_TRUNC('month',ad.created_date) AS month_,
--ad.country_code AS country_code,
approx_distinct(ad.calculation_id, 0.0041) AS count_fraud_calcs,
approx_distinct(ad.ultimate_session_id, 0.0041) AS count_sessions,
approx_distinct(ad.user_id, 0.0041) AS count_users,
approx_distinct(ad.order_happened, 0.0041) AS count_orders,
ROUND(approx_distinct(ad.order_happened, 0.0041)*1.000/approx_distinct(ad.ultimate_session_id, 0.0041),3) order_session_conversion,
ROUND(SUM(ad.price_prediction_eur),0) AS total_price_prediction_eur_GMV,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ad.order_happened IS NULL THEN ad.price_prediction_eur ELSE 0 END),0) AS not_converted_price_prediction_eur,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ad.order_happened IS NULL THEN ad.price_prediction_eur ELSE 0 END)*1.0000/NULLIF(SUM(ad.price_prediction_eur),0),4) AS ratio_GMV_converted
FROM all_data AS ad
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

I received ~40 broken springs from Oslo. All of them have correct wire OD and they all are snapped at the same location. Most likely the issue lies in the material of the spring or heat treatment process of the material.



The spring should last the lifetime of the vehicle, which is 15 000km. If we take an average of applying brakes ever 100m during the ride, it will come out to 150 000k cycles. I propose we do a stress test to check the lifetime of the spring, by setting the benchmark to 150k or failure, whichever comes first.

The testing jig should be made so that multiple springs can be tested simultaneously. 

* If all test samples from LD pass the 150k cycle test, we can assume that it was a batch issue. 
* If the springs fail early in the test, we should run a comparison test with other manufacturer springs (Karasawa, YM, …) to see whether they do better.

{color:#ff5630}*QUESTION FROM POLINA: simply put, the question is: if a passenger is overcharged for a longer route, but they confirmed it was a route they requested - can we refuse to refund them?*{color}



The Passenger terms make it clear that the Fare that is charged to the passenger may change and differ from the estimate provided, see highlighted {color:#ff991f}*orange* {color}text below: 

*PASSENGER TERMS* 

*Clause 15(d).* As part of your request for a Journey, the App will provide you with an estimate of the Fare you will be charged for the provision of the Journey, taking into account any applicable Service Fee and any Toll Charges for the anticipated route. The App may also provide you with an estimate of your arrival time. If the estimate of the Fare changes before your Journey is confirmed, you will be informed of this. {color:#ff991f}The estimates are provided for your reference only and the actual Fare and arrival time may differ from the estimates{color} – for example if you change your destination during the Journey, if the Journey takes materially longer than estimated due to traffic, or due to other factors (e.g. a Toll Charge is applicable due to a change in destination or route). 

*Clause 15(g)(ii)* {color:#ff991f}you can amend your route in consultation with your Driver, in which case, your Fare can change;{color}

[~accountid:5d53a63ba1f3290c16e637d6] The terms and conditions for passengers clearly state that fares may change if the route is amended. Bolt can rely on clauses 15(g)(ii) and 15(d) of the passenger terms and conditions to support this. Therefore, Bolt is within its rights to inform the passenger of the terms and refuse a refund if the fare differs due to the passenger requesting a specific route.

However, I would like to point out to you, that while the passenger can request the driver takes a specific route, the decision is ultimately up to the driver, drivers have autonomy over the route and do not need to agree to any request made by a passenger, see relevant clauses in the driver and passenger terms and conditions: 

*DRIVER TERMS*

*Clause 16.4.* {color:#ff991f}Drivers may fulfil a Journey by any reasonable route{color}, and Bolt UK does not set any route restrictions. Please also refer to the Minimum Service Standards in respect of Journeys in Section 20.

*Clause 28.4.* {color:#ff991f}You may provide a Journey by any reasonable route,{color} and Bolt UK does not set any route restrictions. Please also refer to the Minimum Service Standards in respect of Journeys in Section 32.

*PASSENGER TERMS* 

*Clause 15(g) i.* the {color:#ff991f}Driver can take any reasonable route{color} to your requested destination;

*Clause 15(g) ii.* {color:#ff991f}you can amend your route in consultation with your Driver,{color} in which case, your Fare can change;

I’ve reviewed your ticket submitted to Knowledge Management, along with the most common cases under the Event Category. Here’s what the current KB article contains:

----

The events that *would fall* under {{Driver Fraudulently Asked More Money}} include the following:

* The driver claimed the app did not take or process the in-app payment
* The driver claimed there were app issues or that Bolt is not paying them
* The driver asked to pay in cash instead of in-app and charged the passenger more than expected
* The driver is not happy with the price shown in the app and asks for more money
* The driver claims they changed the payment mode from in-app to cash and demands the user to pay them cash

The events that *would not fall* under {{Driver Fraudulently Asked More Money}} are highlighted in [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/115003285874], and include the following:

* The driver has GPS issues on his phone while using the app which causes multiple extra toll charges. The GPS issues can be seen from Admin
* The rider makes a mistake and gives/sends the driver more money by accident. Then the passenger demands the money back and claims the driver has taken more money
* The driver requests cash for a cleaning fee because the passenger made a mess: cleaning fee disputes should fall under the Price Review procedures
* If the passenger was vulnerable (e.g. intoxicated) and/or the amount requested is considerable, it is *Exploitation of a Vulnerable Person* and the relevant Safety SOP must be followed
* The driver doesn’t accept in-app payments and demands the passenger to pay cash
** If driver asked to pay in cash instead of in-app and the passenger cancels the ride because of this reason, follow the [Rider reports that driver rejected in-app/cash trip|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013784780] guidelines

*If the passenger reports threats from the driver’s side,follow the relevant Safety SOP*

----

Now let me use the examples you provided to KM to illustrate the logic behind the process: overall, if the driver is intentionally lying to the passenger, this is Safety → 

* _If the driver did not notice that the passenger was using a promo code and asked for additional money for the trip, such cases are not considered HP._ → If a passenger uses a promo code, the driver still gets the full price, AFAIK. So if the driver asks for more money than the app shows, this is Safety. 
* _Since there aren’t many requests, it’s important to clarify whether a case should be considered an HP case if the driver requests additional funds for transportation to the correct destination due to a rider's mistake._ → this is Safety as well, all destination changes should go through the app. If the driver did not know of such an app function, they need to be informed. But if the rider reports that the driver was lying about the app features, this is Safety. 
* _The graph shows that the second most frequent request is "Driver asked for extra pay before trip"._ → same here, if the intention of the driver is to lie to the passenger to get more money, this is Safety. 
* _The largest number of tickets relates to double payment. The most common scenario is when a passenger orders a trip for a third person, and the driver collects cash for a trip already paid for by card._ → same here, if the driver is untruthful about the app feature and asks for more money, this is Safety.

This SQL query was used to get the results from Presto/Dbeaver:

{code:sql}select
	a.vertical
	, a.month_dt
	, count(distinct a.order_id) as total_refunds_orders
	, count(distinct case when count_refund_type = 1 then a.order_id end) as count_single_refund_orders
	, count(distinct case when count_refund_type > 1 then a.order_id end) as count_multiple_refunds_orders
	, sum(a.sum_refund_amount_eur) as total_refunded_amount_eur
	, sum(case when count_refund_type = 1 then a.sum_refund_amount_eur end) as single_refunded_amount_eur
	, sum(case when count_refund_type > 1 then a.sum_refund_amount_eur end) as multiple_refunded_amount_eur
from (
		select
			refund_order_id as order_id
			, date_trunc('month',refund_created_date_utc) as month_dt
			, refund_vertical as vertical
			, sum(refund_amount_eur) as sum_refund_amount_eur
			, count(distinct billing_refund_type) as count_refund_type
		from core_models.fact_support_user_refunds
		where refund_created_date_utc >= date('2024-01-01') --refund_order_id = 16149645-- 1968297229--207562342--
		and refund_vertical in ('delivery','rides')
		group by 1,2,3--,4--,5
		order by 3,2 asc,1
	) a
group by 1,2
order by 1,2 asc{code}

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *27 November 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Billing Details*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/sk-sk/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/sk-sk/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

Summary of the payment logic:

Starting from January 2025, we agree to a monthly minimum order of services from NJORD in the amount of €6000 (excluding VAT). If, in any given month, Bolt orders less than €6000 worth of services, up to €3000 of that month’s “unused” amount can be transferred to the following month. This carry-over option is only applicable for one month at a time and does not accumulate over multiple months.

If the Client orders more than the minimum, the Client pays for the actual amount of services provided. Therefore, in practice:

* The minimal monthly invoicing baseline is typically €3000 (excluding VAT).
* If we did not utilize all €6,00 in a given month, and thus have a surplus of up to €3000, that surplus can be carried forward to the next month, increasing the following month’s minimum invoice by that transferred amount (up to a maximum of €3000 carry-over).

NJORD will invoice monthly for the services rendered. Services are billed either at a fixed fee, capped fee, or hourly rate in accordance with the Terms in effect when the services are provided. NJORD will seek our confirmation if the monthly amount of ordered services is likely to exceed €15000 (excluding VAT). Payment terms for invoices are 30 calendar days.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* On 17 December, UK [driver|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/4002488?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] [called|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/490491023] Bolt CS concerned that someone had hacked their account the day before.
** User claims that scammer changed their email address, phone number, and bank details.
** User claims that on 14 December, someone claiming to be from Bolt CS called them to notify them that a customer made a complaint about the user not looking like their profile picture, and that they would send a magic link through which the user could send a picture to verify their identity. Magc link was sent from ‘[ukdriver@bolt-drivers.com|mailto:ukdriver@bolt-drivers.com]’. 
** On 16 December, user noticed they had not been paid, and so they investigated and noticed that their account details had been changed. User has reported this to the police. User has indicated that a payment was sent to the hacker.
* The user has [mentioned|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/490491023] that on 16 December, they spoke to someone else from Bolt CS who restored their email address and phone number. However, bank details still needed to be changed back.
** NB. There are 7 or 8 calls to Bolt CS from the last few days, all of which deal with the same issue.
** User has also confirmed that on 15 December, they got a new phone. 
* Based on review of the user’s profile:
** No driver-rider messages around 14 December that involve sharing contact details / OTP. Last comms were for [this|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/549448411/25?orderTryId=1096566007] trip, and they seem to be genuine. However, various VOIP calls for [this|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/comms-channels/commsHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A%220%22%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22order_id%22%3A549405282%2C%22city_id%22%3A25%2C%22order_system%22%3A%22taxi%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] trip on 14 December.
** On 14 December (20:33, UTC+02:00):
*** Email changed from [worth8788@gmail.com|mailto:worth8788@gmail.com] to [worth8788@tupmail.com|mailto:worth8788@tupmail.com]
*** Phone changed from +447817866270 to +447817866580
** Later that day, new bank statement uploaded.
** On 16 December, phone number and email changed back.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Worth double-checking with InfoSec, but this seems like a case of account compromise. As such, this qualifies as a personal data breach.
* However, it is not yet clear to me if this is a case of UK phishing that we have seen before. The user has thrown a lot of information at us, and it is not yet clear if this case is distingisable.
** If this is a case of UK phishing, we can add it to the tracker.
** If it is not a case of UK phishing, I should prepare a new personal data breach form and escalate to DPO team.
* It seems likely (although details TBC) that the driver has suffered financial detriment. If so, then this likely meets the threshold for A34 notification.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Ask the following:
** How did the scammer call the user? Was this during an active ride?
** Is the email account not one we recognise?
** Has this user ever mentioned being asked for an OTP code?
** Has the scammer been kicked out of the account? Can we be confident the breach is not ongoing?
** Have the bank details been reverted?
** How much financial detriment has the user suffered? Any negative balance on their account?
* Tailor next steps depending on whether this is a similar case of UK phishing or a new / unique one.

(I have not gone through all 70 pages of the Kundeninformation I just scanned it)These are some point that I would suggest to discuss with them, however, most are partly commercial terms so yours to decide, only the 3. point I would highly recommend:

*1. Self-Insured Retention Amount and Monthly Advance Payments*SIR is €10,000 per individual claim under the motor vehicle liability insurance (Section 5.1.2.1).
Monthly advance payments of €150,000 are required for expected claims costs (Section 5.1.2.1 b).
This may lead to:

* High financial exposure due to the large self-insured retention.
* Liquidity constraints if claims volume is lower than expected.

Recommendation:

* Cap the total annual exposure for self-insured retention.
* Include a refund mechanism for excess advance payments.

# *Kasko Coverage Limit*Insurance coverage is capped at €50,000 per vehicle for both Vollkasko and Teilkassko (Section 5.2.2).


Leading to vehicles with values exceeding €50,000 will be underinsured, leading to financial losses in case of damage or loss.

*3. Termination and Renewal Clause*The fleet contract automatically renews annually unless terminated at least one month before the contract ends (Section 2).
Short termination notice provides limited time to negotiate alternative terms or find a new insurer.
Recommendation:

* Lets try to extend the termination notice period to at least 3 months.
* Lets also try to add a clause requiring advance notification from the insurer for contract changes.

You can see how the feature you’re proposing undermines these arguments. 

Thus, my suggestion is to hold off launching this until we have more clarity whether we wish to  increase, decrease or maintain the same reclassification risk profile. The decision on this has not yet been made internally.

Hi [~accountid:6001a724849d640111aa591b] As discussed, I’ll speak to Product Legal about whether we should launch fleets via our updated Bolt Link / Substitution feature as this might be an easier/cleaner way to do this.

After Speaking to Michael Roberts from Product Legal, it is clear that there are legal and finreg issues with launching this fee. 
LEGAL RISKS

* It’s possible that by not collecting such fee for cash rides, it will be considered a card surcharge, which are illegal in most EU countries. It appears that card surcharges are illegal in Ireland, but further assessment can be carried given that FreeNow is operating this way. 
* There is a risk that the technology fee will be considered to form part of the transportation fee in Ireland, which is regulated. However, this can be partially mitigated by keeping the fee flat and low.
* Charging a technology fee to passengers directly may be seen as making drivers subordinated, thereby increasing the reclassification risk. However, this can be partially mitigated by keeping the fee low to potential scrutiny.
* There’s a risk that the fee would aggravate the drivers since they may view it as ‘commission by another name', which could lead to escalation / claims. However, this risk can be partially mitigated by keeping the fee flat and low.

FINREG RISKS

In addition, the key issue is that our current operating structure is not PSD2 compliant since the entity collecting the in app payments on behalf of the drivers is Bolt Operation OÜ (not a local entity). We believe that launching a technology fee increases the risk that our operations catch the eye of Irish Central Bank and this non-compliance becomes evident. 

*That all said, our competitors are charging this fee in Ireland and launching this fee would bring additional 2.1 million in GMV in 2025 alone.  Thus, we should consider seeking external regulatory / finreg advice to speed up the launch of this fee.*

Hi Dawit 



Thank you for the review. 



Points 1 and 2 are actually intentional 🙂 



Point 1

* We are struggling to negotiate a viable/feasible price for the Bolt Drive fleet in DE. That is due to our poor loss history + the fact that fleets in Germany are performing all very poorly loss-wise and, therefore, are a very undesirable risk to insure. We have done calculations and modeling with different payment schemes - and regardless of the high retention this solution seems to be more cost-efficient than other alternatives. 
* If claims volumes are lower than expected - the surplus of our paid retention should carry over to the next period - whereas this is not great cashflow-wise, this is something we have considered, and are willing to accommodate because we have negotiated this whole scheme/setup a lot, other party has accommodated some of our requests, and we will accommodate this request from the other party for compromise. 

Point 2

* We do not actually intend to use the casco policy. We buy casco policy because of a bureaucrautic requirement. In case of accidents, we are prepared to assume the cost of losses. Modelling an actually effective casco policy for such a fleet would be a costly scheme, so we have intentionally asked for high deductibles, to lower the cost of the policy. 

Point 3 

* 30-day tacit renewal clause is highly common with insurance agreements. We start negotiations way earlier than the 30-day deadline. For example, the current policy we have in Germany also includes a 30-day tacit renewal clause, however, we started the procurement process in October, found an alternative more cost-efficient offer (the one in question), and now are changing our suppliers. 🙂 
* Extending the termination notice would actually make things more complicated for us. The 30-day termination clause means that we need to know by 30 October if we want to opt out of the policy or not, with 3-month termination, we would need to know by 30 August if we will want to opt out of the policy. 
* Insurance negotiations are highly affected by claims performance. 30 August is in the middle of Q3 the insurers are unlikely to provide any binding offers with partial claims data. 
* So considering the nature of insurance contract negotiations, I would say that the 30-day term is more beneficial to us than the 3-month term. As we can start negotiating the price as early as we want, the 30-day term is merely for giving our opt-out notification. 



Best

Karmel

Testing started on {{2024-12-16}} 

Following issues so far:

* AIOT MODEL_START parameters were not properly init
* AI_CONTROLLED_ZONE polygons were not prepared&loaded to scooters

After an exhaustive evaluation of the incident’s conditions, these are the evidences/facts

* {{westasia-kafka-1.rides.boltint.net}} got into a _zombie_ and it required forceful restart
* Plenty of Kafka producers experienced random timed-our requests in the time frame between zombie detection and restart
** In the current settings, a timed-out request is retried for 5 times, and considering the request timeout is 30s, a send call is marked as failed after more than 2.5 minutes which is 2.5x than the tolerated interval
** The Kafka Producer treats the time-out error as transient and keeps retrying without marking the broker as down. It only removes the broker when it gets “{{KafkaJSConnectionClosedError}}“. So, the client keeps on targeting the zombie broker which randomly replies.

As per Clause 5.4 of the Partner T&Cs, Bolt has the right to charge a rental or purchase fee for devices provided to partners, That said, since the Special Conditions take precedence over the T&Cs, we would not be able to introduce any such fees unless we first amend the Special Conditions and obtain the partners' consent via signed agreements. Working hypothesis for 566-017: baud rate mismatch

UART in AIoT is configured to 1.5 Mbaud, but actually runs at 1.56 Mbaud (measured using Saleae logic analyzer) - presumably due to sloppy UART driver implementation

UART in IoT is configured to 1.52 Mbaud to fit between requested and actual speed of AIoT. The reason being that if someday the UART driver starts to works correctly, it would not require any changes on IoT side.

Apparently the difference of 40 Kbaud (2.7%) is enough to cause occasional loss of synchronization if the clocks not perfectly accurate.

The Agreement is governed by UK law, but introductory services will be provided in Poland. This agreement can be classified as introductory agency agreement and shall fall under [+Commercial Agents Directive (86/653/EEC)+|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A31986L0653](implemented in the UK laws by [+Commercial Agents (Council Directive) Regulations 1993/3053+|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1993/3053/contents/made]). [Memo|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Bn2zrnrSJHz1a2hWm8ROYCGDYOCB4AfP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=107030908950286443607&rtpof=true&sd=true] on agency agreements.

Main concern is that activity of Bolt can be interpreted as providing financial services or marketing of financial services. To address the concern it is advised to amend wording of the agreement in a way to include provisions that are clearly indicating that Bolt is acting as introductory agent only.

This “[Introduction agency agreement|https://uk.practicallaw.thomsonreuters.com/1-505-2781?originationContext=document&transitionType=DocumentItem&contextData=(sc.Default)&ppcid=2b944e90d8ff481ea9c34827bc472e51&comp=pluk&view=hidealldraftingnotes&firstPage=true&OWSessionId=f3efd795f016409498ee4f9987b70e40&skipAnonymous=true]” was used as an example to propose relevant clauses. It was proposed to include the following provisions:

* definition of introduction
* provision regarding appointment of Bolt to identify Applicants for YouLend in the Eligible Jurisdiction and to make Introductions (as defined).
* provision regarding Bolt having *no* authority to conclude contracts or negotiate them.
* provision regarding Bolt's obligation to disclose its limit on authority.
* provision prescribing that Bolt is entitled to Partner Fee (this is tackled in Annex 1, but I recommend adding it to the main agreement too, calculation can still remain in Annex 1)
* provision regarding YouLend's duty to disclose data about YouLend Financing Agreements concluded with Customers (there is similar wording in 6.2 and definition of Partner Dashboard (which is not used in the agreement), but it is not enough in my opinion, I want it to be more clear).

The provisions were added as follows:

* new definition of "Introduction"
* new clauses 5.1, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8 and 6.11.
* amended clause 9.1.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* On 18 December 2024, UK driver [wrote|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/491479378] to Bolt concerned about their account being hacked.
** On 12 December, user claims they received a call from a Bolt representative who claimed that a rider had reported that their appearance did not match their profile picture. 
*** User was asked to submit a selfie through a ‘secure link’, which the user did.
** On 13 December, user’s account was blocked, and user could not log back in.
** On Monday 16 December, user did not receive their weekly earnings. User claims loss of earnings.
** On 17 December, user visited the Bolt office and was apparently told that their account had been hacked.
*** User claims the hacker changed their phone number, profile picture and bank account details.
* User is alleging negligence / failure to safeguard account and failure to prevent unauthorised payment.
** User requests immediate reimbursement, restoration of their account and a full investigation (including “_an explanation of the steps Bolt will take to prevent similar incidents in the future_”).
** User is threatening to escalate this to data protection authorities if this is not dealt with quickly.
** User demands a response in the next 48 hours.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* This bears similarities with [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-43642|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-43642]. Does not appear to involve requesting OTP details, so we may need to treat this as a new kind of incident.
** However, we still need to confirm first whether: (a) the hacker previously got access to the user’s account and changed their photo, after which Bolt CS genuinely reached out to the user with a magic link; or (b) Bolt CS never actually reached out but rather the hacker sent the magic link. The former could suggest UK phishing, the latter could suggest a new kind of incident.
* I have reviewed the user’s [profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/1062518?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] and can see the following:
** Account is active and blocks appear to have been lifted.
** Various account changes that mirror what the user has said.
*** On 12 December:
**** Email changed from [sfayemi@yahoo.com|mailto:sfayemi@yahoo.com] to [sundayolajide@tupmail.com|mailto:sundayolajide@tupmail.com]
**** Phone changed from +447957109967 to +447957102257
*** On 13 December, new bank statement uploaded, and bank details successfully changed.
*** On 17 December, phone changed back, but email changed again to [syem99@aol.com|mailto:syem99@aol.com].
**** Appears that bank details were reverted on the same day. Password reset link also sent.
** Looking at orders taken around this period:
*** No obvious requests for OTP codes
**** On 11 October, a VoiP call was made from a rider to the user during an active [trip|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/comms-channels/commsHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A%220%22%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22order_id%22%3A548744145%2C%22city_id%22%3A25%2C%22order_system%22%3A%22taxi%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn].
**** Subsequent completed trips on 12 Dec.
**** On 12 October, another VoiP call was made from a rider to the user during an active [trip|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/comms-channels/commsHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A%220%22%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22order_id%22%3A548869717%2C%22city_id%22%3A25%2C%22order_system%22%3A%22taxi%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn].
**** Subsequent completed trips on 12 Dec.
**** On 12 October, another VoiP call was made from a rider to the user during an active [trip|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/comms-channels/commsHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A%220%22%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22order_id%22%3A548921203%2C%22city_id%22%3A25%2C%22order_system%22%3A%22taxi%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn].
**** Subsequent completed trips on 12 and 13 Dec.
*** Given the above, a fraudulent rider could have called the Bolt driver on 12 December and _claimed_  to be Bolt CS, but we currently cannot know for sure.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Confirm with CS:
** Do we have records of Bolt CS calling the user on 12 December?
** Has the driver ever mentioned being asked for a OTP code?
** Is the account currently active?
** Have all steps in KB article been followed? Is the issue no longer ongoing?
** How much was the payout?
* Loop in Kristyna for good measure, and ask is she is aware of any other similar cases.
* Ask InfoSec to review for good measure.
* Tailor next steps depending on whether this is a similar case of UK phishing or a new / unique one.
