We will change the UI for refund actions in Beehive to have some kind of table where agent will select affected invoice rows and enter the amount that will be refunded for the given invoice row. There is no ready design yet.

* *What are the differences between invoice rows?*

Essentially each invoice row corresponds to some component of the final price of the order. We will be using the following data to show for agents:

* title - readable name of the component e.g. "booking fee", "burger", "ridehailing ride", etc.
* type - type of the given invoice row e.g. "delivery_item_food", "ridehailing_booking_fee", etc.
* amount - monetary amount of the given invoice row

+ we can also show how much was already refunded for the given invoice row and maybe some other information if it will be needed. So for instance for delivery order here is how invoice rows might look like:

* burger, delivery_item_food, 5
* fries, delivery_item_food, 4
* delivery fee, delivery_fee, 1



* *How to refund Food Combos?*

If this is just main row with "burger deal" let's say, then agent will select this invoice row, and write down how much for this row should be compensated. Let's say we will compensate 1 eur for missing drink, then it will be "burger deal" invoice row with refund amount = 1. We will have main deal row with the whole price, and explanation rows under it with 0 prices.

Hello,

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.
{color:#bf2600}For issues with refunds from Beehive, kindly reach out to #beehive-agent-support on Slack.{color}

As this subject is high priority for our ops teams in France, please allow me to follow up on this thread to summarise and get aligned on the action points.


# +*The Issue*+*:*

* Women drivers are 3x more robbed, experience 2x more threatening cases, and suffer from 10x more sexual offenses.
* The category right now just “filters” the women, however, it remains too easy for an offender/misbehaving rider to circumvent this. We need to create more friction for it to prevent them from using the category.



# +*The Global intended solution (as you put forward in the thread below)*+*:*

* In short, we’ll be operating selfie+ID checks for riders who want to choose the women category. 
* If the selfie+ID has been recently carried out under a different workflow, we won’t run it again to ensure data minimization. If the selfie+ID has never been verified and the rider does not want to do the check, another category can be chosen.
* The verification is intended to be non-invasive. The AI tool will not be used to scan the face, instead, where possible, the tool will extract the information about the rider’s gender from the identification document. Where it is not possible, a manual check should be carried out. The feasibility of this is in question to implement on a global level. 
* At this stage, without the use of AI to extract gender-specific information or a manual check, a man can book a ride. 

*FR implementation* 

* For the riders who have already verified their ID, for data minimization, Majorel agents will be manually checking all the IDs.
* For new riders, possible use of an external solution that specifically can identify IDs and Passports. 



# +*Concerns to consider*+

* As you have already highlighted, data inaccuracy would be an issue → manual review should rectify this.
* There is a risk of discrimination if the passenger identifies as a woman but their ID has a male identification. Under French law, discrimination is a criminal offence that can lead to imprisonment (Articles 225-1 to 225-4 of the Penal Code).
* We need to be prepared for situations where a woman orders the rider, but she is accompanied by a man - we should consider whether the woman driver has the right to decline service. 



# +*Action points*+*:*

* Ops to implement a process to rectify when a gender is marked incorrectly and needs to be changed;
* With regards to DPA Agreements, we appreciate the need to have the agreements in place with third parties, AI tool providers, and Majorels. Kindly could you confirm if you have already been approached on this point? Has there been any action on this yet? If so, are there any ETAs communicated?
* The Privacy Policy needs to be updated for riders - do we need to wait for Privacy to update the policy before we action anything? Again, any ETAs which can be communicated would be helpful to time manage this launch.
* A continued monitoring from GFT to ensure mitigation against discrimination that constitutes a criminal offence.



Kindly could you share your thoughts on the above actions? and if any action points have been started, can you share any ETAs that you might have to help manage expectations and have a realistic timeline?

Hello [~accountid:61b9ad7c2900b00071da0b68], good morning.

Further to our conversations, I agree that the PT car rental Marketplace (like the car-sharing integration with Miles in DE and with Spark in LT) falls within the scope of the DAC7 under _“rental of any model of transport.”_

Regarding your queries:

* We don´t provide car-sharing services under a principal status in Portugal (i.e., Bolt Drive). The company that provides platform services to our car rental partners (fleet owners) is *Bolt Operations OÜ*, so I agree that this entity should be regarded as the Platform Operator.
* In like manner, *Bolt Ops OÜ* provides platform services to our car-sharing partners in Germany (Miles) and Lithuania (Spark).
* Under the Partnership Agreements with *Drivalia* and *Valpirent* (*PT Marketplace*), _“Bolt is authorised to collect on Partner’s behalf the fees payable by the customers under the Car Rental Agreements, including but not limited to,_ +_fees for the regular use of the Car Rental Service_+_,_ +_recovered damages_+_,_ +_fines_+_,_ +_contractual penalties_+ _and_ +_any other payments made to the Partner through Bolt_+ _by natural persons or businesses (“_*_Fees_*_”), and to forward relevant funds to the Partner.”_
* *Pass through costs*: Although the Agreements concluded with Drivalia and Valpirent do not expressly govern this point, the operations team informed that Bolt will collect costs borne upfront by the partners that are passed through to customers (likewise, in the name and on behalf of our partners), such as traffic fines or the cost of outsourced services.
* *Add-ons*: These are pop-ups in the App whereby the sellers (fleet owners) offer extra items along with the car-sharing or car rental service, such as upgraded insurance, child seats, etc. In like manner, these add-ons allow the sellers to inform the customers about extra costs that may trigger if they cross a border, intercity trips, etc. All revenues that the sellers may realize from the sale of extra items qualify as consideration for DAC7 purposes, and Bolt will collect those revenues in the name and on behalf of the sellers, too. Please keep in mind that such revenues will be included in the invoices that Bolt will issue in the name and on behalf of the sellers.
* I don’t know if the Commerce team is aware of any additional reporting. If you want me to let them know (via slack or ticket) pls LMK.
* AFAIK, we have not formally or officially communicated to our partners that we must provide the tax authorities with information about the type of revenues they realize through the App within the frame of DAC7. Pls note that there isn’t a specific set of Ts&Cs governing Bolt’s relations with the fleet owners, but separate Agreements. The agreements concluded hitherto do not provide for any clause whereby we inform the partners that we must inform the tax authorities in pursuance of DAC7 regulations.

I will be happy to provide further information or any clarification as needed.

 Thank you, and have a nice day.

As I put together a third party workflow for all verticals, I asked Privacy a lot of questions about this. I was told that we are allowed to conduct investigations with the victim, even if they are not the account holder. However, if they do not respond or do not want to speak, we can continue of course with the account holder. 

So, I imagine this works just the same with family accounts. 


* Family owner contacts us about an incident someone in their family had
** We can request to speak with the victim
** If the victim was a minor (a child), we should not speak with them, continue with account holder. 
** If the victim does not want to speak, we just continue with account holder 
** If a victim (not account holder or family owner) contacts us themselves, we can actually conduct entire investigation with them and there is no need to involve the account holder if it is not needed.

*→ 5.89 of the Belgian Civil Code: "Clause exonératoire de responsabilité*

§ 1. Sauf si la loi en dispose autrement, les parties peuvent convenir d'une clause exonérant le débiteur, en tout ou en partie, de sa responsabilité contractuelle ou extracontractuelle.
La clause peut exonérer le débiteur de sa faute lourde ou de celle d'une personne dont il répond. Une telle exonération ne se présume pas.
Sont toutefois réputées non écrites les clauses qui exonèrent le débiteur:
1° de sa faute intentionnelle ou de celle d'une personne dont il répond; ou
2° de sa faute ou de celle d'une personne dont il répond, lorsque cette faute cause une atteinte à la vie ou à l'intégrité physique d'une personne.
Est pareillement réputée non écrite la clause qui vide le contrat de sa substance.
§ 2. Si le débiteur fait appel à des auxiliaires pour l'exécution du contrat, ceux-ci peuvent invoquer contre le créancier principal la clause d'exonération de responsabilité convenue entre celui-ci et le débiteur.

*→  Art. 5.52. Clauses abusives*

Toute clause non négociable et qui crée un déséquilibre manifeste entre les droits et obligations des parties est abusive et réputée non écrite.

L'appréciation du déséquilibre manifeste tient compte de toutes les circonstances qui entourent la conclusion du contrat.

L'alinéa 1er ne s'applique ni à la définition des prestations principales du contrat, ni à l'équivalence entre les prestations principales.

Drivers often don’t understand the difference between account deletion and migration (changing cities or companies). Many request deletion simply because they’ve been told to do so when asking how to move to a new company or why their application wasn’t accepted. This misunderstanding creates unnecessary issues.

Even though we’ve tried to communicate the importance of clearly stating their intent, many drivers still request deletion out of habit or lack of understanding. This highlights the need for a confirmation step to ensure their true intent is captured.

Mistakenly deleting an account due to miscommunication can violate compliance regulations like DAC7. These errors affect tax reporting and create legal risks, even in minor cases. A confirmation step helps prevent such costly mistakes.

Migration between companies or cities happens frequently, and errors in handling these requests cause delays, disrupt operations, and frustrate drivers. A confirmation question avoids unnecessary deletions and keeps the process smooth.

This confirmation step was previously agreed upon with stakeholders and is especially important in regions under DAC7 regulation. This was raised in the past, and then, presumably, deleted. 

We kindly ask you to make the change as soon as possible due top sensitive supply situation, DAC7 regulation and process efficiency.

*Where consent is needed for third party offers? Clarification:*

Where ads are personalised and not direct marketing (i.e., it's an in-app ads banner) - consent does not apply.

Based on the clarification from [~accountid:61cb1160f3037f0069a4cb9e] :

{quote}* _We will use mostly banners for this type of communications - we don’t plan on doing pushes, emails for them in trial phase. They will be present in Bolt Market provider screen and sometimes (less than 5% of the cases) in Bolt Food homepage._{quote}

Its going to be in-app, and thus, consent should not apply.

Where the promo is direct marketing and is regarding a third party (i.e. not promoting offers available in Bolt Market from merchants / offers from restaurants in Bolt Food) - these should be categorised as Third Party promotions and direct marketing must be sent only based on consent.

*Do we need consent for marketing personalisation?*

We do not normally ask consent for marketing personalisation - only exception is the use of live location data for direct marketing personalisation - in this case, consent is required. But this is only in Rides, afaik. If we plan to use any sensitive/special categories of data for marketing personalisation, consent may be needed, but this is assessed on a case-by case basis

                tao.driver_id,
                tao.rider_id,
                ta.status as anomaly_status,
                ta.support_case_id,
                tickets.value as ticket_status,
                rider_status.change_reason as rider_answer,
                driver_status.change_reason as driver_answer

          from ng_public.trip_anomaly_trip_anomaly ta

          join ng_public.trip_anomaly_order tao

          left join ng_public.trip_anomaly_client_status rider_status

The Number Node can only output hardcoded values: 

* number (when explicitly defined) or 
* null (when not defined). 

There are likely pipelines based on this hardcoded null, so if we simply force the node to have a number value, those pipelines will break, and we’ll also need a new node of type null.

A possible solution is to automatically detect those pipelines and (automatically or manually) replace such nodes with a Null Node. 

Another solution is to dynamically change the Number Node's output socket type based on whether it has a value inside.

Probably other solutions exist.

As regards Bolt's obligation to provide uninterrupted access to the platform, then in the PA and OA, there is only one provision stating Bolt's obligation regarding the software in Clause 5.5 of PA and Clause 5.1 (h) of OA:
"_Bolt shall do everything reasonably possible to provide the flawless performance of Bolt Software. Bolt shall within a reasonable time (a) respond and eliminate all defects in regard to Bolt Software, and its functionality, and (b) upon the first request of the Partner, correct any false or misleading information about the Partner. Except as expressly stated in this Agreement, Bolt expressly disclaims all warranties and conditions with respect of Bolt Software."_

In short, Bolt does not have an obligation to provide uninterrupted access to Bolt software, i.e., the Bolt platform; no SLAs and no warranties are provided by Bolt regarding platform availability.

*Bolt Lux Legal Considerations*

Bolt Lux implies higher quality standards (e.g., clothing, behaviour, higher AR, and possibly a no-ride cancellation policy), thus will require enhanced driver supervision -> increased reclass risk

*(i) Legal Framework* (a bit of theory)

* Under EE law there is a presumption of employment, characterised primarily by the *employer’s management and control.* The degree of subordination is a critical factor.
* To refute this presumption, the *alleged employer must demonstrate that the alleged employee was largely independent* in deciding the way, time, and place of performing work.
* Establishing employment requires a *holistic assessment* of all circumstances. In disputes, the Labor Dispute Committee or the court evaluates whether an employment relationship exists.
* The actual intent of the parties is assessed and matters. If the intent is unclear, the contract is interpreted as a reasonable person in similar circumstances would have understood it. Thus, it must be *shown that the mutual intent of Bolt and the driver was to establish a service agreement*, not an employment agreement.

*(ii) Practical part*
*Legal Enforcement of Bolt Lux* 

Given the above, there are two approaches:

# *B2B Agreement with Fleets*
## *Traditional fleets:* Sign an SLA with fleets specifying KPIs and quality standards. The fleet becomes responsible for ensuring KPIs are met, typically through their employees. Supervision will be exercised by the fleet, not Bolt.
## *Non-traditional fleet:* In EE, we don't have traditional fleets. Instead, non-traditional fleets (car rental companies) rent vehicles to independent drivers. Thus:
### Bolt could sign an SLA with a car rental company that has vehicles that meet Bolt Lux requirements.
### The car rental company determines how to ensure these KPIs are met, for example, by signing an  SLA to the car rental contract with independent drivers who qualify.
### The car rental company supervises these drivers to ensure compliance with Bolt Lux standards.
### Risk: the car rental company could be deemed the employer; Bolt the same faces risks if it collects and evaluates driver performance data (direct supervision.)
# *Direct Employment by Bolt*
## Removes labour law risks but is the most burdensome option, especially for a test period, and is not currently supported by the business.
## But FYI - Bolt previously considered building its own fleet and employing drivers. Therefore, in EE a separate legal entity *Bolt Fleet Services EE OÜ* was created (currently dormant and not in use). This idea could be revisited if similar quality initiatives are launched on a larger scales.

*Test Period*

To simplify the test launch, the business could proceed with a "gentlemen’s agreement" with selected fleets and drivers as mentioned by [@oscar.room|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U0545A2GTS6]and [@aleksis.anijarv|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U0762KSBTQF], ensuring:

* Bolt Lux KPIs and quality standards are tied to the category, not the individual driver
* Drivers who qualify for Bolt Lux can freely opt-in (they can also refuse to do so)
* Drivers can opt out of Bolt Lux at any time without consequences
* If a driver fails to meet Bolt Lux requirements, they are removed from the Bolt Lux category but continue providing services on Bolt’s platform as usual.

For testing purposes, these terms could be communicated to drivers via email. If the test proves successful, Bolt Lux could be formally launched using the simplest legal model, as outlined in *Option 1.b*.

*PR Considerations* 

* Even on a limited scale, Bolt Lux is likely to draw attention. To preserve Bolt’s "platform" narrative, it is advised to prepare responses to potential questions about the legal nature of driver engagement in advance.
* The employment status of platform workers is a hot topic across the EU, and LT and LV drivers are closely following developments in EE. For example:
** A group of LT drivers has threatened to file a claim in Estonian courts, alleging Bolt employs them in LT.
** LT labour authorities have launched an investigation into Bolt’s relationship with drivers.

News spreads quickly in the Baltics, so pre-prepared arguments can help prevent complaints. Even one dissatisfied EE driver is enough to submit a claim to EE labour inspection and potentially trigger a broader investigation.
I hope these concerns remain theoretical, but being prepared will help us feel more confident and secure.

# The shareholders of the Company pass a resolution (typically a written resolution) ("*MCR*") to authorise the BOD to proceed to allot and issue shares.
# The investor (i.e., the person making the cash injection to the Company) executes a share application form provided by the Company evidencing its agreement to take up the shares and remit the cash injection to the Company (typically by wire transfer evidenced by the Company's bank statement confirming receipt of the funds).
# The BOD passes a subsequent DCR to approve the allotment and issuance of shares once the remittance of the share capitalisation moneys is received by the Company.
# The Company issues a letter of confirmation and provides the evidence of remittance to the company secretary so that the company secretary can proceed to formalise the share capitalisation exercise.

# The company secretary updates the register of members of the Company (“*ROM*”) and submits the notification of the update of the ROM to the CCM within 14 days from the allotment.
# If required, the company secretary issues new share certificate(s) to the investor in accordance with the Company's constitution.

Hey!

After gathering information regarding this predicament, I think there are no easy solutions here.

Essentially, yes we could sign the liability agreement, but it would not be enforceable and should there be any disputes, it will be stuck down by the courts.

Why?

* VS pay is low;
* We cannot deduct more from the pay than the subtraction between their pay and the minimum pay.
* The liability agreement caps the maximum sum we can claim from the employee. If the cap is at 4000 EUR and a premium vehicle is a total loss, then we’re still taking in the loss.
* We have to pay for the agreement. And the payment must be in line with the risks associated with the liability.
* The payment must be in line with the industry risks and insurance practices. As we don’t have voluntary property insurance (kasko), the courts will say that we tried to use our employees as minimum-pay-insurance-product; essentially placing operational risks on the employees.
* The tl;dr of the opinion of the national court is that the compensation for this agreement should be higher than the insurance premiums per vehicle. If I recall correctly, our rates are somewhere ~360 EUR per vehicle per month. Essentially, somewhere 400 EUR per month of additional payment would be in order. This would be a ~30% wage increase for the VS.



Essentially, we have to pay. There is no way around this. And this would be a paper tiger without any real-life power.

In my opinion, there is one workable solution here. If we have to pay and we’re willing to pay, I’d go another route: a bonus system.

* The same amount we’d add as an additional payment for the liability agreement will be booked as a bonus payment.
* We can set the conditions for the bonus payments. One of the conditions will be that there are no damages to the vehicles during employee’s operations.
* If there are any damages, then it will be deducted from the “bonus” fund.
* For the bonus to be payable, they have to be employed for at least 2/3 of the FY.
* This would give us the option to pursue a damage claim if the damages are high. 
* If there are no deductions, the person would receive their yearly bonus somewhere in Q1. If there are damage claims, the amount will be deducted and maybe even nullified.

The notification in the Privacy Notice is not enough in this case due to the following:

* *Privacy Notice is a broad statement* of how we process the data of couriers. We do not put detailed information about Acceptance Rate that is necessary for transparency with couriers, eg we will not mention how this is calculated, what % they need to have to not receive less orders and what their current AR is. This is not the information for the Privacy Notice.
* We recommend putting *this statement directly in the Bolt Courier App as this gives more transparency required by the regulators in such cases (according to the fine given to our competitor).* 
** We show to couriers the percentage of their AR directly in the Bolt Courier App and we call it Acceptance Rate there. 
** We propose to put a short notice under this section: '_Your Acceptance Rate may affect the number of orders you receive. If your Acceptance Rate has fallen below [X]%, you will receive fewer orders until it rises above [X]%. To improve this, simply accept more orders to increase your Acceptance Rate.’_ 
* If the very activity and the notification pose a risk from the reclassification side, is this better  to consider removing it from high-risk reclassification countries rather than hide it given privacy and legal risks?
* We also believe that the lack of transparency affects not only privacy but can also be taken into account for the reclassification case.

What do you think? How high is the risk from your side for these countries?

## *Note, however, that our (white label) financial services partners may need to do similar checks for the purposes of offering payments under license to transportations service providers (Airwallex soon in Canada), for offering cards to our corporate customers (Marqeta soon for Bolt Business  expense management cards), for offering lending to restaurants (YouLend soon in Poland). This is generally an obligation of our financial services partner. In case they want to use our help, this would be specifically agreed in the cooperation agreement, and they would ultimately be reliable for making sure those checks are done compliantly. If we are involved, the data we collect may also concern directors, other representatives, UBOs of our customer
# [~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117] is owning this topic, and [~accountid:712020:e33d3b05-13ba-4374-b342-d0e2cc8272e7] from my team is making sure also AML/CTF/sanctions regulation driven things are properly covered the contractual relationships we will put in place. That’s WIP, so I am not sure about the final setup
# Yes. 
## Taiwan is a fleet market, meaning legally the fleet is selling transportation services to rider. Usual scenario is that platform needs to conduct AML/CTF/sanctions checks to sellers (however, that also includes obtaining certain data about fleet company’s directors, other representatives who may act based on POA, and UBOs). 
## *Note: To understand fleet’s activities, then to some extent we have to also monitor driver specific data. E.g. if our systems see that a single driver connected to a fleet is doing more volumes on the platform than practically logical, this can indicate that this driver is faking rides, which often relates to an attempt to max out fraudulent cards. Other than being fraud, this would also qualify as laundering of money - making funds gained as a result of illegal activity (card fraud) seem legitimate (payout from Bolt). So, the same info we now process for fraud management, would also be processed with the purpose of applying AML/CTF checks.
## As a rule, we do not apply AML/CTF/sanctions checks to buyer side (riders or in the future Bolt Business customers). However, this may be relevant, if for some reason they cross the statutory thresholds which trigger the obligation to also apply controls to buyer side. The thresholds are quite high and we will put technical controls in place, to prevent us exceeding those, so we hope practically we will not need to apply those. But in rare cases where our logic/controls may fail, we should have a right to process data also for buyer side AML/CTF/sanctions checks (the obligation for which, again, derives from the law). 
# What exactly you mean here? I have never seen any AML/KYC checks agreements being concluded with company’s directors, other representatives who may act based on POA, or UBOs. That’s also not practically logical. There must be another way to solve this
## E.g. all EU financial service providers (banks, payment institutions, credit providers etc) apply exactly the same AML/CTF/sanctions controls as we plan in Taiwan, including they often engage external auditors to comply with their legal obligation to conduct internal audits.

The issue was because of too little memory for the PreLive containers. It had only 90MiB so processing even 9MiB attachment could cause the out of memory error. Because of this error the message about a new unread email got stuck in the SNS queue an when the process is recovered it tried to process this message again and crashed and went on and on. 

On Live the containers are configured to have 440MiB, so it was never a problem there.

As a solution we increased the container size to have 300MiB which should be enough for emails up to 25MiB attachments, which is the maximum attachment size allowed by Gmail. 

Beehive had the very same issue if a user attaches a file of a big size (about 7-10MiB) to the support case email. Probably they have never tested attachments of such a big size, so this issue was never reported to us.

Hey, [~accountid:615af98d07ac3c006800769e].

Coming back to you on your question. 

I discussed this with our Process Excellence, Training, and Quality teams, and we concluded that it is quite a _grey area right now_. We talked about what would make the most sense since, as you mentioned, the current closing note template references only one Event Grouping and Event Category. So, if 2 or more ECs are reported in a safety event, *the closing note should refer to the EC with the highest Risk Type.* 

It’s clear that we shouldn’t disregard the other reported ECs, as that might affect precedent counting in future safety cases, leading to incorrectly applied consequential actions. However, the additional ECs should be mentioned in the initial note/comment, which means the information is still available.

* The Product team is going to work on automating comments in Rides cases. If developed and implemented successfully, this will alleviate the manual input currently required for safety case documentation.
*  All the safety internal notes and Admin comment templates will be reviewed thoroughly to determine which elements are really needed and to align on the most appropriate format. We will definitely consider the point you have brought up about how to properly document a safety case where more than 1 EC is reported.  

At this time, I can’t give you a specific ETA on these initiatives, but I can reassure you that we’re working on it. 🙏 



I hope this answers your question, or at least gives a better clarity. If there’s anything else or you have additional questions, feel free to raise them in a new ticket. 

Thank you, and have a nice day! 🙂

Hi Philippine,

Thanks for looping us in. {color:#4c9aff}*Are you able to provide a bit more context behind what is driving this initiative*{color}? What are the specific reasons why we want to lobby for safety processes like verification and dashcams to be mandatory?

By way of brief overview:

* From a Privacy POV, we would not be against lobbying the French government in this way, provided that we lobby for the French government to make these processes mandatory through *_national legislation_* (rather than e.g., a municipal decision). The key consideration here is that the processes should be required by law, so as to make our compliance position clearer and more defensible.
* Ultimately, you will need to *_check with the Product / Leadership team_* whether they would be happy to push forward this this, as they may object.
* I summarise below some of the key Privacy considerations relating to these two processes, which aligns with the position taken when these processes were proposed in the past.

*Rider Verification*

* {color:#ff5630}[Gab to insert some points]{color}

*Dashcams*

* We would *_not_* recommend *_requiring_* drivers to install dashcams in their cars (unless this became a mandatory legal obligation).
** We have taken the position that drivers are independent controllers of any footage recorded on their dashcams - this position allows us to sidestep a lot of privacy law issues that would otherwise arise, and is one we recently reiterated to the Estonian regulator. 
** In order to be able to maintain this position, we need to be able to demonstrate that we do not exercise any control over the use of the cameras - requiring drivers to install dashcams could undermine this position.
* Where dashcams are installed in Bolt cars, we should ensure that the following are in place:
** *We should not have access to dashcam recordings by default* - again, this position allows us to sidestep a lot of privacy law issues that would otherwise arise.
*** This can be distinguished from where dashcam recordings are submitted to us after a safety incident happened (our position here is more defensible as we would be investigating a safety event).
** We can *_encourage_* drivers to have a *sign / sticker* noting that the passenger is being recorded, but we cannot *_require_* drivers to have this (unless this became a mandatory legal obligation).
*** Again, we need to be able to demonstrate that we do not exercise any control over the use of the cameras, which would be undermined if we required signage / stickers to be in place.
*** Instead, we should remind drivers to comply with applicable laws when installing dashcams in their cars.
